extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and appellants handling appeals before the Board (Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences / PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules in the MPEP for handling Board decisions (including remands, new grounds of rejection, rehearing, amendments in conformity, publication/public access, and examiner actions after Board decisions). Covers appellant options, timing, and examiner/TC/Office actions following Board rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand decisions not final for judicial review (37 CFR 41.50(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision of the Board which includes a remand will not be considered final for judicial review; following conclusion of proceedings before the examiner the Board will either adopt its earlier decision as final for judicial review or render a new decision based on all appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a remand is included the Board’s decision is not final; final action by the Board (after remand proceedings conclude) gives rise to the alternatives available to an appellant following a Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of appeals pending related court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may refuse to consider an appeal until conclusion of a pending civil action or appeal to the Federal Circuit involving identical or similar issues; such suspension is recognized as sound practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appellant is not entitled to use prolonged pendency of a court proceeding to avoid res judicata and relitigate the same or substantially the same issue in another application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withhold mailing of decision to permit refiling
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may petition that the decision be withheld to permit refiling of the application at any time prior to the mailing of the decision; up to 30 days may be granted though time is usually limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board more prone to entertain an early petition which obviates necessity for oral hearing or setting hearing date; if case already set for oral hearing petition should request vacating the hearing date, not postponing it. Petitions filed same day decision mailed to withdraw appeal will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board statement on how a claim may be amended (37 CFR 41.50(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board’s opinion may include an explicit statement of how a claim on appeal may be amended to overcome a specific rejection; when such a statement is included appellant has the right to amend in conformity with it, and such amendment will overcome the specific rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment in conformity with the Board’s explicit statement will overcome the specific rejection. The examiner must ensure the amendment actually conforms. The Board’s making of such a statement is discretionary; an offhand remark that a feature does not appear in a claim is not to be taken as authorization to amend unless the Board expressly states so (ex parte Norlund). The right to amend under 41.50(c) may be exercised only within the period allowed for seeking court review under 37 CFR 1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds of rejection by the Board (37 CFR 41.50(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has knowledge of grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include a statement to that effect with reasons, which constitutes a new ground of rejection; such a new ground is not final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Board makes a new ground the appellant, within two months from date of decision, must either (1) reopen prosecution by submitting appropriate amendment and/or new evidence so the matter is remanded to the examiner, or (2) request rehearing addressing the new ground and stating with particularity points misapprehended or overlooked. If appellant does not act, appeal as to those claims terminates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extension limits for Board-related time periods (37 CFR 41.50(f) & 41.52(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the time periods set forth for actions under 41.50 and 41.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may only be obtained under 37 CFR 1.136(b), or under 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination appeals. Practitioners must rely on the limited extension routes specified rather than 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to reject allowed claims is discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Board is authorized to reject allowed claims, this is not intended as instruction to examine every allowed claim; authority exists to act when it becomes apparent allowed claims may be subject to rejection on same or different grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise of authority under 41.50(b) is discretionary; failure to exercise discretion should not be construed as an implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to Board actions (37 CFR 41.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Board action is available for public inspection if rendered in a file open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11 or in an application published under 37 CFR 1.211–1.221. The Office may independently publish any Board action available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Board actions not publishable under the above, the Director may publish if special circumstances warrant; a party may object within two months on trade-secret/confidentiality grounds and must specify deletions. The party will have time (not less than 20 days) to seek reconsideration and court review before contested portions are made public over objection. The record of the proceeding is available unless the patent application is not otherwise public; after final Board action the record becomes public if the file becomes open or the application is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of proceeding to examiner after Board decision (37 CFR 41.54)
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, the proceeding will be returned to the examiner, subject to appellant's right of appeal or other review, for further action by appellant or examiner as required to carry into effect the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the decision is mailed to appellant and the original placed in the file; the Board notes the decision in the file and record of appeals and forwards the file to the examiner immediately if all rejections are reversed, and after about 10 weeks if any rejection is affirmed (or after decision on rehearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and timing after Board makes a new rejection (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Board makes a new rejection under 41.50(b), appellant may (A) reopen prosecution (amendment/new evidence) or (B) request rehearing; the amendment/new evidence or rehearing request must be filed within 2 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant submits amendment/new evidence as to less than all rejected claims and requests rehearing for the remainder, the examiner will not consider claims for which rehearing was requested; argument not accompanied by amendment/new evidence will be treated as rehearing request. The 'new evidence' may be a showing under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an 'appropriate amendment' under 41.50(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is 'appropriate' if it amends one or more of the claims rejected, or substitutes new claims to avoid the art or reasons adduced by the Board; such amended/new claims must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment that merely adds new claims without amending or substituting for the rejected claims is not appropriate; new claims with argument will not be entered and should be treated as a rehearing request. If examiner deems amendment/new evidence not to overcome the rejection, he/she will again reject the claims (possibly finally).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument without amendment/new evidence treated as rehearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant submits argument without either an appropriate amendment or new evidence as to any of the claims rejected by the Board, it will be treated as a request for rehearing under 41.50(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for rehearing accompanied by an appropriate amendment and/or new evidence will instead be treated as a submission under 41.50(b)(1) (reopening prosecution) rather than a proper rehearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and consequences of prosecution reopened only as to new rejection subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection raised by the Board does not reopen prosecution except as to the subject matter to which the new rejection was applied; an affirmed rejection in the Board's decision remains not open to further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution before the examiner of the 41.50(b) rejection can incidentally result in overcoming an affirmed rejection even though that affirmed rejection is not open to further prosecution. If prosecution does not overcome the 41.50(b) rejection, applicant may file a second appeal limited to that rejection, requiring new notice of appeal, brief, and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing request content and limitations (37 CFR 41.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the original Board decision; the request must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked. Arguments not raised in the briefs and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in the rehearing request except as allowed by specific provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New arguments are permitted only (A) upon showing good cause based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision, or (B) as new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection under 41.50(b). Rehearing is normally on the written record (not oral). The decision on rehearing incorporates the earlier opinion except portions specifically withdrawn, and the rehearing decision is final for judicial review except when otherwise noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing is not entitlement to oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'rehearing' should not be interpreted as meaning appellant is entitled to an oral hearing on the request for rehearing, but only to rehearing on the written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the normal practice of the Board to grant rehearings in the sense of another oral hearing (citing ex parte Argoudelis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when reversed in whole (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reversal of the examiner’s rejection brings the case up for immediate action by the examiner; the examiner should not regard such reversal as a challenge to make a new search to uncover other references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second examiner should give full faith and credit to the prior examiner’s search. If the examiner has specific knowledge of reference(s) indicating nonpatentability of reversed claims, submit matter to Technology Center Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198; TC Director approval is placed on action reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requests for rehearing and internal approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request rehearing of the Board decision; such a request should normally be made within 2 months of receipt of the Board decision in the TC and must be approved by the TC Director and forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval before mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must state with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked; arguments not raised in the answers before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted except upon showing of good cause to present a new argument based on a recent relevant decision. The request should set a 2-month period for appellant to file a reply; if approved, TC will mail copy to appellant and after reply period the file is forwarded to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of withdrawn appealed claims (cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appellant withdraws some of the appealed claims (claims subject to a ground of rejection that appellant did not present for review in the brief) and the Board reverses the examiner on the remaining appealed claims, the withdrawal is treated as an authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must notify the appellant of cancellation of withdrawn claims (see MPEP § 1215.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when no claims stand allowed (abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no claims stand allowed after Board decision and the time for seeking court review has passed without review, proceedings are terminated and the application is to be stamped abandoned and sent to abandoned files; in ex parte reexamination a reexamination certificate should be issued under 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate conversion or abandonment when dependent claims were allowable only because of dependency on rejected independent claims. Examiners must follow specified approaches (convert dependent to independent by examiner’s amendment and issue, or set a 1-month time to rewrite dependent claims in independent form with no extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a); failure results in abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when some claims stand allowed (issue/certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims stand allowed the appellant is not required to file a reply; the examiner issues the application or ex parte reexamination certificate on the claims which stand allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For paper files, draw a red-ink line through refused claims and write 'Board Decision' in margin. If Board affirmed independent claim and reversed dependent claims, examiner may convert dependents into independent form by examiner’s amendment, cancel the independent claim with affirmed rejection, and issue application with allowed claims; alternatively set a 1-month time for appellant to rewrite dependent claim(s) to independent form (no extensions under 1.136(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and timing for rewriting dependent claims when independents cancelled
rubrics_metrics.description: When independent claim(s) are cancelled by examiner in accordance with MPEP § 1214.06, applicant is given ONE MONTH from mailing date to present dependent claim(s) in independent form to avoid abandonment; NO EXTENSIONS under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply will result in cancellation of the dependent claims and the application will be allowed with specified claim(s); the MPEP provides form paragraphs (¶ 12.119.01, ¶ 12.119.02) for examiner use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period to correct formal matters when period for seeking court review has lapsed
rubrics_metrics.description: When the period under 37 CFR 1.304 for seeking court review has expired and no further action taken by appellant, the proceedings as to rejected claims are terminated and the application will be passed to issue on allowed claims provided formal matters are promptly corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant required to correct outstanding formal matters within a shortened statutory period set to expire ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from mailing date to avoid abandonment. Extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136 for these formal corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims that require action after partial affirmance/reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: If Board decision is affirmance-in-part and includes a reversal that brings certain claims up for action on the merits, the examiner will take up the application for appropriate action on those matters; the application is not open to further prosecution except as to such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers instances like reversal of generic claims, unelected species, etc.; examiner must take appropriate action limited to the matters brought up by the reversal.
